findings.quote: Intro paragraph 2 and Takeaway: 'will not reach plan fiduciaries until mid-2027 or 2028 depending on the plan year'; also 'once an employer's plan year begins on or after July 1, 2027, the disclosure mandates become legally enforceable'
findings.problem: Unsupported timing inference. Paragraph (e) requires disclosure reasonably in advance of entering, extending or renewing (90 days deemed reasonable for renewals), so first disclosures can precede July 1, 2027 or Jan 1, 2028. The rule gives no first-disclosure date.
findings.fix: State that the rule gives no calendar date; earliest covered plan years begin July 1, 2027, calendar-year plans first become covered Jan 1, 2028, and fiduciaries could see disclosures before those dates.

findings.quote: How Disclosure Could Reach Copays Indirectly: 'an employee paying 20 percent coinsurance pays a share of that elevated list price'
findings.problem: The 20 percent figure is not in the preamble but sits in a sentence attributed to the Department.
findings.fix: Remove the figure or label it a hypothetical in a separate sentence.

findings.quote: FAQ: 'The rule does not explicitly define spread pricing, but treats it as a category of compensation.'
findings.problem: Contradicted by paragraphs (e)(3)(ii)(A)(3) and (g)(2)(ii)(A)(3), which define spread compensation as the per-drug difference between what the plan pays the PBM and what the PBM pays the pharmacy.

findings.quote: FAQ: 'The rule applies only to large self-insured group health plans.' and Takeaway 'applies only to large self-insured plans' (CR-A2)
findings.problem: Paragraph (b) qualifier absent from FAQ and Takeaway; (b) excludes only fully insured plans and affiliated-sponsor plans.
findings.fix: State specified large employer / specified large plan with both exclusions; say the Department describes the result as large self-insured plans.

findings.quote: Who This Is Not For: 'workers in smaller self-insured plans sponsored by businesses with fewer than 100 employees do not receive the detailed fee schedules'
findings.problem: Workers never receive these disclosures; the real tests are 100 average employees under IRC 4980H aggregation or 100 participants.
findings.fix: State the 4980H aggregation and participant tests; add employer size to the HR question.

findings.quote: First mentions of ERISA, IRC section 4980H, 29 U.S.C. 1002(16)(B), Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 unlinked
findings.problem: Named laws must link to a primary source on first mention.

findings.quote: Meta description 'go to employer plan fiduciaries, not workers' and body 'disclosed to the employer's plan fiduciary, not returned to participants'
Body prose rhythm: 104 of 126 sentences long, repeated 10-sentence all-long runs, many over 30 words
findings.fix: Vary real sentences; split overloaded ones.

findings.quote: 'If a provider discovers an error, it must correct the disclosure within 30 calendar days'
findings.problem: Paragraph (l) is a good-faith safe harbor, not a freestanding duty.

consequentialClaims.quote: The initial disclosures will not reach plan fiduciaries until mid-2027 or 2028 depending on the plan year
consequentialClaims.reason: Timing claim contradicted by paragraph (e) advance-disclosure language (finding 1).
